deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages): A is a small category, X a topos, and φ: A → X a functor, written α ↦ U_α. Three hypotheses are in play. Hyp 1: the U_α cover e_X. Hyp 2: for α, β, the U_γ, over all spans α ← γ → β, cover U_α × U_β. Hyp 2': for every cospan α_1 → α_0 ← α_2, the U_γ, over commutative squares completing it, cover U_{α_1} ×_{U_{α_0}} U_{α_2}.

Grothendieck rephrases these through the colimit-preserving extension φ_!: A^ → X (left Kan extension along Yoneda, φ_!(F) = colim_{A/F} U_α). Since φ_! commutes with colimits, a covering family of the form ∐ U_γ → (target) is the same as saying that a canonical comparison map out of φ_! of a presheaf limit is epi:
(a) φ_!(e_{A^}) → e_X is epi;
(b) φ_!(α×β) → φ_!α × φ_!β is epi, for α, β in A (product taken in A^);
(c) φ_!(α ×_{α_0} β) → φ_!α ×_{φ_!α_0} φ_!β is epi, for every cospan in A.

He then notes the pleasant case: φ_! is left exact, i.e. φ_! = f* for a geometric morphism f: X → A^. This is the Diaconescu / SGA4 IV correspondence between flat functors and points-type morphisms. In that case the maps in (a)–(c) are isomorphisms. He presumes the converse: (a)–(c) being isos forces exactness. The proof sketch writes each presheaf as F = colim_{A/F} α and uses universality of colimits in both toposes. The next page carries this out, extending (b) and (c) to arbitrary presheaves (b', c') and hence to all finite limits. It then asks whether the epi form of the hypotheses can hold without φ_! being exact, and when.

Purpose: in the 'topos stratifié' project, families of open subobjects U_α indexed by a category or poset of strata should define a morphism X → A^ (a 'stratification' of the topos X). The page sorts out whether the natural covering axioms already amount to flatness.
errors:
The epi conditions (a), (b), (c) are strictly weaker than flatness, i.e. internal filteredness of φ. The standard third axiom is the equalizer one: for u, v: α ⇉ β, the U_w with uw = vw cover Eq(U_u, U_v). Grothendieck's cospan condition does not imply it.

Counterexample: A = BG for a nontrivial group G, X = Set, φ(*) = a point. Then φ_!F = F/G. Conditions (a), (b), (c) hold (all targets are points, all sources nonempty). Yet φ_! does not preserve products: (G×G)/G has |G| elements.

So the answer to the question raised on the next page ('can the hypothesis be satisfied without φ_! being exact?') is yes, as long as the condition is only required to be epi. The equalizer condition is the missing ingredient.
For posets A (or when the U_α are subobjects and A is thin), the equalizer condition is automatic. There (a) and (b) epi already give internal filteredness, hence exactness.

The converse 'iso in (a), (b), (c) ⇒ φ_! left exact' is presumed, not proved here. It is plausible, since injectivity in (b) and (c) recovers the missing equalizer information, but the 'trivial' colimit argument needs care with images and monos. Not a demonstrated error, only a gap.

ideas.what: Reformulating covering conditions on a functor A → X as epi-ness of φ_! on terminal objects, products and fibre products of representables
ideas.modern_name: internally filtering / flat functors into a topos
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exposé IV (flat functors, points of toposes)

ideas.what: φ_! left exact ⇔ φ_! = f* for a geometric morphism f: X → A^
ideas.modern_name: Diaconescu's theorem / universal property of presheaf toposes

ideas.what: Checking left exactness of φ_! only on finite limits of representables (terminal, binary product, cospan)

missed.claim: Grothendieck uses a cospan-cone axiom in place of the equalizer axiom and asks when the epi conditions hold without flatness. The answer is: whenever the equalizer condition fails, e.g. A = BG. For posets of strata the issue disappears. This is a well-known subtlety, not a new result.
missed.quote: Mais cette hypothèse peut-elle être vérifiée, sans que φ_! soit exact : Quand ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginally: relative and weak flatness notions (Karazeris, Caramello) already cover this ground.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine re-derivation of the flat-functor / geometric-morphism correspondence in a stratification context. The only point of interest is the use of a cospan axiom instead of the equalizer axiom, which is a known subtlety.
